chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about oil and butter, two for one. He said, 'Hand to hand, there is no objection to it.'

key_terms.اَلزَّيْت: Oil (specifically olive oil in this context)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging oil and butter in different quantities according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that exchanging oil for butter in a 2:1 ratio is permissible provided the transaction is 'hand to hand' (yadan bi-yadin), emphasizing the condition of immediate possession to avoid riba al-fadl. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between specific commodity exchanges where unequal quantities are allowed if the medium of exchange is the same, ensuring the transaction remains free from usury. The emphasis on immediate exchange underscores the practical application of Quranic prohibitions on riba in daily commercial activities.
